content.value_statement: WooCommerce contributors need project-specific commands for testing and code quality. This skill provides focused workflows for tests, linting, formatting, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Selects focused PHP unit test commands by class, method, directory, or name pattern.
Guides JavaScript test execution, watch mode, file targeting, and coverage checks.
Explains branch-scoped PHP and JavaScript linting commands and automatic fixes.
Provides WooCommerce PHP style patterns for comments, headers, alignment, parameters, and indentation.
Provides JavaScript and TypeScript localization patterns for plurals, placeholders, links, and translator comments.
Guides Markdown linting, UTF-8 checks, code fence fixes, line wrapping, and spacing.
limitations: Requires a local WooCommerce repository with its dependencies and test environment configured.
Does not replace test design, code review, or manual validation of business behavior.
Commands can vary when WooCommerce scripts or repository structure change.
Automatic lint fixes may modify files and still require review before commit.

use_cases.title: Validate a PHP change
use_cases.description: Choose focused unit tests, run branch-level PHP linting, and review failures before committing.

use_cases.title: Check localized interface text
use_cases.description: Review placeholders, plural forms, translator comments, linked text, and relevant JavaScript lint commands.

use_cases.title: Prepare documentation updates
use_cases.description: Run repository-aware Markdown checks and fix code fences, line length, spacing, and encoding issues.

prompt_templates.title: Run one PHP test
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the command to run the WooCommerce PHP test class [class name]. Explain how to read a failure.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a focused test command.

prompt_templates.title: Check changed files
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WooCommerce quality check sequence for my changed [PHP or JavaScript] files. Include tests, branch-scoped linting, and review steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A contributor wants a pre-commit workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Fix localization lint errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this localization issue: [error and surrounding text]. Recommend the correct placeholders, translator comments, plural handling, and targeted lint command.
prompt_templates.scenario: A frontend developer is resolving i18n errors.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a failing development cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this WooCommerce test and lint output: [output]. Separate root causes, propose focused commands, and order fixes to minimize unrelated changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced contributor needs coordinated troubleshooting.

output_examples.input: I changed one payment test class. What should I run?
output: Run the PHP test environment with a filter for the changed class.
Run branch-scoped PHP linting after the test passes.
Review automatic fixes and rerun the focused test before committing.

output_examples.input: My translated React string contains a link and a brand name.
output: Use a placeholder for the brand name.
Use an interpolated element for the link.
Add a translator comment directly before the translation call.
Run ESLint only on the relevant file.

output_examples.input: Markdown linting reports fence and line-length errors.
output_examples.output: Run the repository-configured automatic fix first. Then add language labels, wrap prose, verify spacing, and rerun the targeted check.

best_practices: Run the smallest relevant test set during development, then broaden validation before committing.
Use branch-scoped or file-specific lint commands to avoid unrelated changes.
Review every automatic fix and rerun affected tests and checks.
anti_patterns: Do not lint the entire repository when only branch changes require validation.
Do not commit automatic formatting changes without reviewing the diff.
Do not hardcode translatable brand names or interpolate variables without translator context.

faq.question: Which languages and file types does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers WooCommerce PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Markdown testing or quality workflows.

faq.question: Can it run every command automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and workflow guidance. Execution depends on the connected agent, repository access, and local permissions.

faq.question: Does it configure the WooCommerce test environment?
faq.answer: It documents environment commands and troubleshooting, but the repository and required dependencies must already be available.

faq.question: Can it fix lint errors?
faq.answer: It recommends targeted automatic fixes and manual patterns. You should review changed files before committing.

faq.question: Does it support localization work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers translation functions, plurals, placeholders, linked text, brand names, and translator comments.

faq.question: Should I run checks across the entire repository?
faq.answer: Usually no. Use branch-scoped or file-specific commands unless full validation is required.
